title: Strict KEX: connection survives a first packet other than KEXINIT
quote: Because the message that signals support for strict KEX is enabled by the SSH_MSG_KEXINIT message, implementations MUST verify that the SSH_MSG_KEXINIT was the first message received from the peer. / This includes terminating the connection if the first packet received is not SSH2_MSG_KEXINIT.
rationale: Violation: the first packet the mapper puts on the wire is not KEXINIT, and the connection survives the client KEXINIT (which carries kex-strict-c-v00@openssh.com), the client NEWKEYS, and then the server sends a real message without closing. The check may be retrospective, so silence on the stray packet and termination up to the client NEWKEYS are fine; NO_CHANNEL steps send nothing and do not count as a first packet. Revised 2026-11-07: the earlier version stopped at the client KEXINIT and flagged libssh 0.12.2, which disconnects at NEWKEYS.
